🎨 ABOUT OPENART

OpenArt is an AI storytelling and visual creation platform used by millions of creators worldwide. We're building the next generation of creative tools powered by cutting-edge AI — enabling anyone to create videos, visuals, characters, and stories with unprecedented speed and imagination.

We believe the future of creativity is AI-native, and we're shaping that future.




🚀 WHY JOIN OPENART

 - Ground floor of a new category — help define what "agent" means for creative work, the way Director redefined what "directing" means for video.

 - Small team, massive surface area — engineers own real systems end to end, not slices.

 - Real scale, real stakes — your agents run for millions of creators, and what you ship shows up in the product within days.

 - AI-native product — you'll help decide how frontier models get orchestrated and exposed as experiences that feel effortless rather than technical.

🎯 ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring engineers to build the agent layer behind OpenArt's next generation of creative products, starting with Director — which lets anyone "vibe direct" a multi-minute cinematic video by chatting with AI. You'll be building the agent infrastructure that pushes experiences like this further: longer-horizon planning, tool use across multiple model vendors, memory across sessions, and the harness that keeps all of it reliable in production.

This isn't a research role — it's a product-and-systems role. You'll build on and extend the agent harness (tool use, context management, multi-step planning, evaluation), develop the MCP servers and CLI tooling around it, and ship the frontend experiences that make all of it feel effortless rather than technical. You'll work closely with the founders, the agent team, and design to turn "what should this agent be able to do" into a system that actually does it — reliably, at scale.




🛠 WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and extend the agent harness that powers OpenArt's conversational and autonomous creative workflows: tool use, context/memory management, multi-step planning, and sub-agent orchestration

 - Build and maintain MCP servers and CLI-based agent tooling that connect our agents to internal services, external model vendors, and creative asset pipelines

 - Author reusable Agent Skills and structured workflows that let agents reliably handle complex, multi-step creative tasks — scene planning, storyboarding, asset generation, revision loops

 - Contribute to evaluation frameworks and observability so the team knows when an agent is working well, and can catch regressions before users do

 - Ship polished, production frontend experiences (React/Next.js) for agent-driven products, end to end

 - Make pragmatic trade-offs between speed, correctness, and scalability — and communicate them clearly

 - Partner closely with product, design, and GTM to translate user needs into technical solutions

 - Track the fast-moving agent ecosystem (MCP, Agent Skills, orchestration frameworks) and bring the best of it into OpenArt's stack
   
   


⚙ WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Core Requirements

 - 2+ years of full-stack engineering experience shipping production software

 - Hands-on experience building LLM-powered agents or applications that have reached real users — not just prototypes or demos

 - Working familiarity with agent harness concepts: tool use, context/memory management, multi-step planning, or sub-agent orchestration

 - Solid data modeling and schema design skills for real product use cases

 - A strong AI-assisted coding practice — you use tools like Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor as a core part of how you build, and have real opinions about what makes them work well

 - Product sense — you think about what makes an agent experience feel trustworthy and delightful, not just functional

 - Clear communication — you can explain agent behavior and technical trade-offs to teammates who aren't engineers

Nice to Have

 - Experience authoring reusable Agent Skills or structured agent workflows

 - Practical experience building MCP servers or CLI tooling for agents

 - Exposure to agent orchestration frameworks (Claude Agent SDK, LangGraph, or similar) or LLM evaluation / observability tooling

 - Hands-on experience with image / video generation models

 - Startup experience, or having built something 0 to 1 (side projects count)
   
   


💰 COMPENSATION

 - Equity - meaningful ownership in what you build

 - High autonomy, high growth environment
   
   


🌍 WORK SETUP

🎯 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN 3–6 MONTHS

Every company runs on its people, and the software that manages them is some of the oldest in the enterprise. Incumbents like ADP and Workday built their businesses on complexity and large ops teams. Warp is built for AI to be the primary operator. Every advance in LLM capability widens our lead.

We process $X billion in annual payments for high-growth companies across all 50 US states + globally.

We've raised $85M from Battery Ventures, Sapphire Ventures, Peak XV, Sound Ventures (Ashton Kutcher), and Y Combinator, alongside operators including Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Claire Hughes Johnson (Stripe), and the founders of Dropbox and Replit. Our team comes from MIT, Ramp, Brex, Google, Gusto, Rippling, and more.

We hire people who ship constantly, own outcomes, and care about craft. If you want to automate an entire category of work that every company depends on, this is the place.

About the Role
High-growth companies spend thousands of hours on people operations: onboarding new hires, running payroll, managing benefits, provisioning devices, answering policy questions, approving time off and expenses. Most of that work still runs on spreadsheets, tickets, and people chasing people. We're building agents that do it for them.
Warp Agent works in the background for HR, finance, and people teams. It gets new hires ready for day one, reviews expenses against policy, handles time-off requests, checks payroll before it runs, and reports on what's happening across the company. Customers hand it a receipt or a notice and it takes care of the rest. Because Warp runs the full employee lifecycle on one platform, the agent has the context to finish the work, not just suggest it.
The hard part is trust. People data is the most sensitive data a company has, and people operations leave little room for error. Every agent action respects role-based permissions, so an IT manager's agent can provision a laptop without ever seeing anyone's salary, and every action is logged and auditable.
We believe agents will soon do more work on Warp than people do. As an Applied AI Engineer, you'll build those agents, the runtime they operate on, and the systems that make them reliable enough to run a company's people operations.


What You'll Do

 - Ship agentic features end to end, from the model call to the UI, across HRIS, payroll, benefits, IT, and more

 - Build and extend Warp Agent's harness: tool-calling, durable execution for long-running work (triggers, scheduling, wait and resume), and a run log that makes every agent action auditable

 - Design evals and guardrails for workflows where mistakes are costly, and decide when an agent acts on its own versus asks for approval

 - Build new agent workflows and expand what customers can configure and author themselves

 - Extend our permission model to agents so every action respects who the agent is working for

 - Build internal agents and tooling that remove manual work across Warp's own teams

 - Build new surfaces for interactions with Warp agent across the web app, employee app, mobile app, and slack

 - Collaborate directly with the CTO and CEO

You'll Be Good for This Role If You

 - Have shipped LLM features that real users depend on in production, and know where they break

 - Think in systems: evals, observability, cost, latency, and failure modes

 - Are product-minded and care how an agent's work shows up for the person who delegated it

 - Get excited by hard domains where correctness matters more than demos

 - Use coding agents heavily in your own workflow and have opinions on what works

What You Need

 - Strong full-stack engineering skills and expertise in a modern, strongly typed language

 - A track record of building production AI systems: agents, tool use, retrieval, or structured extraction

 - Experience designing reliable backend systems

 - High agency. You figure things out.

 - Willingness to work from our NYC office five days a week
